evidence: Read CONTEXT whole (section 'Capacity before content', closing on the REMEMBER paragraph), then the draft, which sits once in that last paragraph and joins 'Not everything in hypnotic imagery is literal,' to 'especially if it has to do with trauma or memories.' without a grammatical seam. Against SOURCE: the middle sentence 'The mind makes it symbolic, squashes things together, distorts, dramatizes, pulls from cultural influences, fears etc.' is word for word the approved one; the two swaps are 'relates to trauma and memory' -> 'has to do with trauma or memories' and 'So, treat it like an image and get some help outside of yourself!' -> 'So take it as an image and get some outside help!'. That is exactly what the_change says (Emulate's end of the first sentence and last sentence, middle stays). Meaning: 'and' -> 'or' and 'memory' -> 'memories' make the 'especially' trigger a little wider (trauma, or memories in general) than the joint reading of 'trauma and memory'. I judged that inside the meaning: 'especially' is emphasis, not a rule; the same section already says 'show me the memory'; and his published guide says the result of imagery is 'symbolic information or a hypothesis, never proof of history'. 'outside help' keeps the point of 'help outside of yourself' in a plainer idiom, and the caution keeps the same strength. No new claim, fact, first-person statement or named entity (C03, C04 absent); 'it' keeps the source's referent, the hypnotic imagery (C02 absent); no 'the kid' (C01 absent). Voice and seam: 'has to do with', 'take it as' and 'get some outside help!' are plain and casual and fit the section's exclamation-and-etc. voice; I felt no seam at either splice, no tidy summary and no hedge he would not write. Tell rows: went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 on the draft in its context; none is present that the change introduced. Considered T29 for the 'So' closer: by the inventory's test the paragraph without it ends on a list and never says what to do, so the last sentence adds a directive (outside help) instead of restating; absent. The writer's ledger says this passage is not the end of its section, but in CONTEXT it is the last paragraph, so I judged T28 myself: the closer is a caution, not healing, uplift or a summary of what the reader learned, and it is the approved paragraph's own ending; absent. T02: the claim, mechanism list, instruction cadence belongs to the approved paragraph, is one short note and not a run of compressed commands, and the change does not alter its structure; absent. T15: the swaps go to plainer, more common words, not rarer synonyms, so this is not the humanizer-reword operation; absent. T26: 'symbolic' recurs from 'in symbolic form' earlier but carries the same idea, and 'etc.' recurs through the section as his voice, inside the unchanged sentence; absent. T13 and T09 (the D9 pointer): the unchanged mechanism list is where the paragraph notices something specific, and it gets more room than the other two sentences, so neither is present. Linter findings: B4/E15 flags the six-item sentence, which is unchanged from the approved source and is an open list ('etc.') of distinct ways the mind alters an image rather than a packed argument, and the change did not make it, so accepted. D9 is what a sentence-level swap in a three-sentence paragraph gives (same points, same order), and each part has its own job (qualifier, mechanism list, what to do), so accepted. O45 flags the closing caution, which is already in the approved paragraph (batch 470) and is reworded in place at the same strength; nothing safety-related is added or repeated, and it tells the reader what to do with the image they just got, so accepted. If Joel wants that caution cut under O45, that is a decision about the approved paragraph, not about this wording change.
